steps.text: Place sweet potatoes in a large stockpot; cover with 1 inch of water. Bring to a boil over medium heat and cook until fork-tender, about 20 minutes. Drain, cool, and remove skins.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease or butter a 2-quart casserole dish.
Place potatoes in a large bowl; beat with an electric mixer on low speed until potatoes begin to break up. Increase speed to medium-high; continue blending until smooth.
Reduce speed to low and add white sugar, milk, 1/2 cup butter, eggs, vanilla extract, and salt; continue mixing until well combined.
Remove and discard any potato fibers on the beaters. Pour mixture into the prepared casserole dish.
Mix brown sugar, pecans, flour, and 1/3 cup butter together in a medium bowl until crumbly. Sprinkle topping over potato mixture.
Bake in the preheated oven until center of soufflé is set, about 40 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Sweet Potato Soufflé
raw_recipe.description: This sweet potato souffle made with mashed sweet potatoes is light and fluffy with a crumbly pecan topping—perfect for Thanksgiving.

review.reviewBody: I think this is a really good recipe...but, I would improve on it by simply separating my egg yolks and whites. Then, I would add the yolks in with the other ingredients while mixing. Next comes the main difference - beat the egg whites until stiff ( not dry ), and gently fold them into the sweet potato mixture. Bake immediately after topping. Add marshmallows the last 15 minutes of baking. ( Do not open oven while baking and handle casserole carefully as this is truly a souffle with the eggs added this way. ) I KNOW you will love it prepared in this manner. Enjoy! Barbara / Fountain Inn, SC

This recipe turned out great after a little changes: 1) I used brown sugar in the sweet potato mixture, but not a full cup - about 1/2. 2) A HUGE time saving trick (as I was making an entire Thanksgiving dinner for 8 people) was that I used 2 packages of Ore-Ida's frozen bagged sweet potatoes (near the frozen french fries in my grocery store). Prepared them in the microwave as directed on the package instead of using fresh sweet potatoes. I'm confident no one even noticed and it saved a lot of time. 3) I also used a little cinnamon, nutmeg, and all spice in the sweet potato mix. 4) I will probably double the topping portion next time as it didn't come close to fully covering my pan.

As soon as I read to "boil potatoes" I knew that - from personal experience, family feedback, taste preferences - I'd be baking the potatoes. (And yes, there really is a taste difference even though the soufflé will be baked again later.) I also added cinnamon (1.5 teaspoons) and ginger (1/3 teaspoon) to the recipe for more flavor.

This easy is so easy to follow. I did take the suggestion of one reviewer to beat the egg whites separately and fold them into the sweet potato mixture. I used heavy whipping cream instead of milk, a pinch of cinnamon and nutmeg. It turns out so fully and delicious! I will be making this dish for Thanksgiving this year!
family loves this. I add an additional egg and beat eggs with sugar til frothy then add potato, etc.

This recipe is as good as everyone says!! So great!! I did change it a bit because it is sooooo super sweet!! Here is what I did and everyone at Thanksgiving dinner loved it. I took out the white sugar in the main recipe and replaced with just 1/4 cup of maple syrup. Still sweet enough- really- I also used 1/4 cup milk and 1/4 cup cream. Not sure if it really made a difference, it was really light and creamy however. For the topping I only made half the recipe and used only half the brown sugar. This is my new must bring dish. YUM

I made this dish a number of times years ago and was looking for the recipe. I remembered while assembling the dish that if you bake the sweet potato until soft, it adds a very sweet flavor. I do not add any sugar to the souffle mix and only 1/2 cup brown sugar to the topping. Also, if the butter is fairly soft, the flour, brown sugar and nuts mix better and puff up nicely. I also use double strength vanilla. These changes were made after people would say they like the souffle but it is too sweet. I get requests for it often now.

My husband and I loved this because we love sweet potatoes but it was much too sweet (also used candied pecans instead of regular). I will be making it again, however next time I will cut the sugar in the recipe by 1/2 and also beat the egg whites and yolks separately and much more to increase the airiness.

I love this recipe. I've made it for the past 4 years at Thanksgiving and its always a hit. The only change I make is to bake the potatoes and not boil them. I think you get a lot more of the natural sugar out of them this way. I also top it with marshmallows the last 10-15 minutes.

This recipe is amazing! I baked my potato son the oven for 50 minutes. I also added 2 tablespoons less sugar. This recipe is amazing!!!! I made a vegan version by using flaxseed instead of eggs and vegan milk and butter. I can't get over how well this tastes! Just like the honey baked ham store ????????
Great recipe, but to make it exceptional use evaporated milk instead of regular milk. Also bake your potatoes instead of boiling. The flavor is definitely better.
This receipe was spot on. Great side dish.
Prepared as written, too sweet for us!
Only change I made was double the amount of cinnamon. I'm a cinnamon junkie. Added nutmeg. First time making soufflé. Made with my 7 yo grandson. Was a HIT!!!
The his recipe is perfect as is. My family loved it!
Great recipe
Very easy to make I can't.

I have to agree with the other reviewers, that when made as written, this sweet potato souffle is too sweet. I think I would take another reviewer's advice and just add a little maple syrup (along with some cinnamon and nutmeg) to the sweet potato filling, and then only have the brown sugar on top. I think that balance the sweet a bit better. Otherwise, it was nice texture with the smooth sweet potato filling to the crunch topping. I would make it again with adjustments. Thank you for sharing your recipe!
Loved it!!! Always a family favorite during the holidays.
It was great 👍😃
